notes:
SCCM Retro 2.27.0 - The PS2 Update

A new PlayStation 2 engine, and it is the default.

* New PS2 engine: ARMSX2, a native build with real ARM64 recompilers.
  Graphics-heavy scenes run up to a third faster than AetherSX2 with the
  new GS back thread, and save states, hotkeys, and overlays all work.
  This update installs the engine on every console automatically.
* We fixed the emulator itself: two engine bugs that erased menu and HUD
  text in the Jak series (and likely other games) were found and patched
  by SCCM in the emulator source. Jak II now renders perfectly, including
  at full speed with the back thread on. Both fixes have been offered to
  the ARMSX2 project.
* The engine is now profile-guided: we rebuilt ARMSX2 tuned by real
  gameplay recordings from this exact hardware. Heavy scenes run up to a
  third faster on top of everything above; several rooms that used to
  struggle now hold a locked 60.
* One PS2 tab again. Every PS2 game gets an "Emulator engine" selector in
  its Performance settings: ARMSX2 by default, AetherSX2 as the legacy
  choice for games that misbehave. Switching engines also switches which
  settings the menu shows. Your per-game tuning, favorites, playtime, and
  save states carry over automatically.
* New in the pause menu: "Emulation settings" under Performance. Change
  EE cycle rate, cycle skip, blending, effects accuracy, screen sync,
  deinterlacing, resolution, aspect ratio, and mipmapping LIVE while the
  game runs. Changes last for the session; your saved per-game settings
  stay untouched.
* New per-game levers on the ARMSX2 engine: "Screen sync" picks between
  tear-free vsync and full-speed-with-tearing per game, and "Effects
  accuracy" speeds up draw-heavy games. Its "Batched" setting is another
  SCCM emulator patch: it keeps dynamic lighting fully correct while
  drawing it a smarter way, worth about 17% in the heaviest rooms.
* Performance settings are reordered with the biggest levers first, each
  with a one-line hint on when to use it.
* PS2 quality of life: screen tearing fixed (proper vsync), per-game
  internal resolution up to 4x, wider blending accuracy range, and the
  FPS overlay now follows the overlay toggle instead of always showing.

The engine adds about 45 MB to this update, one time.
